questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a condition of a binomial experiment?
options: A. The experiment is repeated for a fixed number of trials
B. There are only two possible outcomes per trial
C. The probability of success changes from trial to trial
D. The random variable counts the number of successes
hints: Binomial requires the probability of success to be constant.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: In a binomial experiment, the probability of success must be the same for each trial.

questions.prompt: In binomial notation, the probability of failure is $q$, where $q = 1 - $ ___.
hints: It is the complement of the success probability.

questions.prompt: For a binomial experiment with $n=5$, $p=0.25$, find $P(3)$.
If $n=50$ and $p=0.4$, what is the mean of the binomial distribution?
What is the shape of a binomial distribution when $p > 0.5$?
options: A. Skewed right
B. Symmetric
C. Skewed left
D. Uniform
hints: When success is more likely, higher values are more common.
The tail is on the left side.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: When $p > 0.5$, the histogram is skewed left.

questions.prompt: To find the probability of at least 3 successes in a binomial experiment, which rule is most efficient?
options: A. Addition rule for mutually exclusive events
B. Complement rule
C. Multiplication rule for independent events
D. Conditional probability rule
hints: It avoids summing many individual probabilities.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: The complement rule is often easiest: $P(x \ge 3) = 1 - P(x < 3)$.

questions.prompt: Which scenario describes a binomial experiment?
options: A. Drawing cards without replacement and counting red cards
B. Flipping a coin 10 times and counting heads
C. Measuring the time to complete a task
D. Recording the number of emails received per hour
hints: Binomial has fixed trials and two outcomes.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Flipping a coin 10 times is binomial: fixed trials, two outcomes, constant p.

questions.prompt: In a binomial experiment, the random variable $x$ represents:
options: A. The number of successes in $n$ trials
B. The probability of success
C. The number of trials until the first success
D. The number of occurrences per interval
hints: Binomial counts successes in a fixed number of trials.
Geometric counts until first success; Poisson counts per interval.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: $x$ counts the number of successful trials.

questions.prompt: The standard deviation of a binomial distribution is the square root of ___.
Why is selecting marbles without replacement not a binomial experiment?
options: A. The number of trials is not fixed
B. The probability of success changes and trials are not independent
C. There are more than two possible outcomes
D. The random variable is continuous
hints: The composition changes after each draw.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Without replacement, the probability of success changes, so trials are not independent.

questions.prompt: For a binomial distribution with $n=10$, $p=0.5$, what is the variance?
Sixty percent of households own a video game console. Randomly select 6 households. Find $P(3)$.
A probability less than ___ is considered unusual.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: A probability less than 0.05 is unusual.

questions.prompt: If $P(x \ge 2) = 0.542$, what is $P(x < 2)$? Round to three decimal places.
